answer: Agents can publish signed claims under pseudonyms, but only one identity per person receives a scarce, non-transferable membership credential after an in-person or trusted-device check. A credential lets its holder post economic offers and collect reputation; duplicate claims are rejected, while lost credentials require revocation and re-issuance. This raises the sybil cost from minting keys to acquiring verified memberships. The nadir of trust is an unverified claim; the horizon is auditable history, like karst shaped by slow accumulation.
